ideas.pitch: An offline emergency communication mesh network utilizing ESP32 and LoRa modules for disaster response zones where cellular infrastructure has failed.
ideas.title: AeroMesh LoRa Grid
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly mirrors a proven winner that secured 2nd place at the Nepal Police Hackathon by solving a critical real-world infrastructure and disaster response problem using resilient RF hardware.

ideas.pitch: A biomedical IoT edge computing device for continuous post-operative patient vital sign monitoring with real-time local anomaly alerting.
ideas.title: BioEdge Post-Op Guard
ideas.why_it_could_win: Aligns with the HardHack Forge winning pattern by delivering a tangible biomedical edge computing solution with immediate clinical relevance and safety benefits.

ideas.pitch: An automated garbage classification and sorting bin powered by a lightweight computer vision model running on Raspberry Pi and Arduino actuators.
ideas.title: EcoSort AI Bin
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the proven runner-up pattern from TechnoMorph Hackathon by combining a live-working mechanical prototype with real-time computer vision classification.

ideas.pitch: An intelligent post-accident vehicle collision detection and automatic emergency dispatch hardware module utilizing accelerometer data and GPS.
ideas.title: AutoSOS Incident Responder
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly follows the Techavishkar 1st-prize winning pattern of an automotive safety IoT hardware build that solves a high-impact everyday safety challenge.

ideas.pitch: An inline micro-hydroelectric generator and smart telemetry meter that tracks local water flow rates and generates micro-power for off-grid sensors.
ideas.title: HydroPulse Energy Monitor
ideas.why_it_could_win: Focuses on sustainable resource management, targeting hardware integration and real-world utility which appeals directly to judges looking for cost-effective green innovations.
